chunks.text: I was 28 when Dev held up my pay stub and asked me one question. "Who's keeping the difference?" I didn't know what he meant. Then he pointed at one line, and my stomach dropped. For three years, I'd been turning down free money.
And the worst part? I did it to impress people I barely knew. Let me take you back.

Twenty-five. First real job. Forty-four thousand a year, and I felt like I'd made it. So I did what felt right and leased a brand-new car, four hundred and eighty-nine dollars a month. Not because I needed it.
Because I wanted everyone in that parking lot to think I was doing great. On day one, HR gave me a folder.

Somewhere on page six it said the company would match every dollar I put into my retirement plan, up to four percent of my salary. I never got to page six. I picked two percent, because two sounded responsible, and the lease sounded urgent.
